newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 13.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- HALEWOOD FEARS AS FORD WARNS ON COSTS

Ford yesterday announced it was considering rationalising its European operation, raising fears over the future of its plant at Halewood, Merseyside. European losses for the company in the third quarter rose from US$320 million to $470 million.
-- BRUSSELS BACKS AID PACKAGE FOR BELFAST TEXTILES

The European Court has approved government aid for a Northern Ireland textile project after rejecting industry complaints that EU assistance rules were breached. The decision means construction of a 157 million pound stg plant near Belfast by Taiwanese conglomerate Hanlon can go ahead, although the 61 million pound aid package may need renegotiation. The plant will create 1,800 jobs.
-- POLLY GROUP'S RIGHTS CHALLENGE

Voyager, an Isle of Man-registered company and subsidiary of Polly Peck International, is taking Turkey to the European Court of Human Rights for blocking the recovery of its assets since Polly's 1990 collapse. The British administrator, Chris Barlow of Coopers & Lybrand, is supporting Voyager in its action.
THE TIMES
-- PEARL CUSTOMERS MISS OUT AS AMP PLANS TO FLOAT

AMP, the largest life assurance society in Australia, has announced flotation plans that will offer 2.3 million members shares worth an average of 4,300 Australian dollars. Some 200,000 UK members of London Life and AMP (UK) Ltd will also be eligible, but policyholders with non-mutual Pearl Assurance will not. The proposal will be put to a vote next year.
-- GREENALLS POURS 175 MILLION POUNDS INTO PUB EXPANSION

Pubs and hotels company Greenalls Group is to create about 1,000 jobs through a 175 million pound-investment in its pubs estate. It plans to open about 230 new outlets next year. The announcement came as the company said its pre-tax profits were up 48 percent to 149 million pounds in the year to 27 September.
-- GAGGING ORDER FOUGHT BY LONDON ELECTRICITY CHIEFS

London Electricity is fighting a Takeover Panel gagging order as speculation continued over its links with Northern Electric, facing a hostile US bid. London Electricity said it was banned from business comment other than its brief results statement made yesterday, as the panel had declared it to be in an offer period three weeks ago. The panel said a bid on London by the US company Entergy was still possible.
THE GUARDIAN
-- TOP FINANCIER SUSPECTED OF HELPING INSIDER DEALERS

A top finance official is suspected of being the main source of price-sensitive information passed to a possible City insider-dealing ring. A full inquiry by the Department of Trade & Industry is trying to discover links between the corporate financier, who cannot be named, and the most prolific member of the suspected dealing ring.
-- WICKES HOPES TO REBUILD ITS PROFITS THE DIY WAY

Wickes, the DIY retailer, yesterday launched a rescue share issue to restore its finances damaged by the 42 million pound stg fraud discovered this summer. The company says it is to concentrate on getting the chain back to profitability, while analysts believe its best hope for the future lies in being taken over. The company has acknowledged that it has received expressions of interest from potential buyers.
-- M&G PUNISHED AS INVESTORS PULL OUT

M&G, one of Britain's biggest independent fund managers, said yesterday unit trust investors had cashed in about one-tenth of their holdings. The company said it had been punished for its disappointing year by a record number of customers cashing in their investments. Its policy of investing in high-yield stocks and smaller companies was not the only factor in a bad year that left it among the worst performing in the unit trust industry last year. It also claimed to have experienced a small sell-off around the time of the Morgan Grenfell affair, as some investors mistakenly assumed the two were related.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- GUINNESS REPORT LIKELY TO SLATE TOP CITY FIGURES

A Department of Trade and Industry report on the Guinness affair is expected to be strongly critical of several leading City figures. The report is to be published within days of a ruling by the European Court of Human Rights on whether accepted civil liberties were infringed in prosecuting Ernest Saunders, the former chairman of Guinness. Government sources say the report will be published regardless of whether the European Court favours Mr Saunders.
-- SPENDING TRIGGERS INFLATION FEARS

The latest figures from the CBI suggest buoyant consumer spending is bringing the prospect of higher inflation and imports, and a strong pound is starting to hit exports. Many economists now believe that interest rates should go up if the government is to hit its inflation target. Export orders are at their lowest in nearly three years.
-- INDEPENDENT DIRECTORS BEEF UP LME REGULATION

The London Metal Exchange is expected to strengthen its board with an increase in independent directors and setting up an information sharing arrangement with the Securities and Futures Authority. Although in the absence of changes in the Financial Services Act, the LME or the SFA cannot require all metal traders in London to become members of the exchange.
